instruction: Adjust the title font size on slide 1 to 72pt and on slide 5 to 48pt.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing title font sizes: slide 1 to 72pt (914400 EMU) and slide 5 to 48pt (609600 EMU). The evaluator extracts title font sizes from slides 1 and 5 and verifies they match the expected values within 2% tolerance. Verified original sizes: slide 1 is 108.5pt, slide 5 is 65pt.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Proportional score: 0.5 for slide 1 correct, 0.5 for slide 5 correct

llm_judge_reasons: Complete coverage: Evaluator checks both requirements (slide 1 to 72pt and slide 5 to 48pt)
Correct getter logic: Extracts title font sizes from slides at indices 0 and 4 (slides 1 and 5)
Correct metric logic: Compares actual vs expected font sizes with 2% tolerance
Correct expected values: 914400 EMU = 72pt, 609600 EMU = 48pt (conversion verified)
Proper parameter handling: Metric correctly accesses expected.get('sizes') since expected IS the rules dict
Appropriate postconfig: Saves file with Ctrl+S before reading to ensure fresh state
Proper partial credit: Proportional scoring (0.5 per slide) makes semantic sense
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Title detection uses heuristics (placeholder type 1/3 or first shape with text > 5 chars) which could fail if title has ≤5 characters and is not a placeholder. This is acceptable for typical presentations but could be more robust.
Minor: Font size extraction takes only the first run's font size. If title has mixed font sizes, only first run is checked. This is acceptable for typical uniform-formatted titles.
